title: GETS — Group-wise Ensemble Temperature Scaling for NBA Calibration
problem: Current fleet Brier is 0.22159 (S15 best). All islands use tree ensembles (XGBoost, CatBoost, RandomForest, ExtraTrees) with no explicit post-hoc calibration. Miscalibrated probabilities inflate Brier score unnecessarily.
solution: Apply GETS (Group-wise Ensemble Temperature Scaling) as a post-hoc calibration step after GA evolution selects the best model. GETS extends classical temperature scaling by learning separate temperature parameters per group of ensemble members, correcting systematic over/under-confidence in different probability ranges.

phase1.description: Add calibration wrapper to engine.py evaluate_individual()
phase1.method: CalibratedClassifierCV with isotonic regression (5-fold) as baseline
phase1.notes: Isotonic regression is the best non-parametric calibrator for tree models per 2025 research

phase2.description: Implement temperature scaling as post-processing on top GA individuals
phase2.code_sketch: def temperature_scale(logits, T): return logits / T; optimize T via Brier score on holdout set
phase2.notes: Temperature scaling cannot hurt Brier score when T is optimized on val set

phase3.description: Implement GETS: group by model_type (xgboost/catboost/rf/et) and learn per-group T
phase3.benefit: Allows systematic correction — CatBoost systematically over-confident vs RandomForest
phase3.expected_gain: 0.002-0.005 Brier improvement on top of baseline

existing_work_in_repo: calibration/ directory exists, probability-clipping-brier-2026-03-28.md and temperature-scaling-calibration-2026-04-03.json proposals exist — this builds on those, adds group-wise extension
notes_for_implementation: Calibration must be computed on holdout (not training) set — use last 2 seasons as cal set
Temperature T is a scalar — no new model weights, just divides raw logits
Must be applied AFTER GA selects winners, not inside the GA loop (avoid leakage)
Apply to ALL 6 islands but tune T independently per island
Cross-check: calibrated Brier must be <= uncalibrated Brier, else revert
references: GETS: Ensemble Temperature Scaling — ICLR 2025 https://openreview.net/pdf?id=qgsXsqahMq
Stacked ensemble NBA 2025 — Nature Scientific Reports https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-13657-1
